title: Everyday Situations: Choose What Happens Next
summary: Three common situations: feeling forgotten by family, a new health worry, and an invitation to a gathering. The person chooses, sees what might happen, and the psychologist leads the discussion.
clinicianNotes: Original scenarios and conversation starters. They are not a measure of mental health. Written for adults aged 60 and over. Draft content: needs review by a licensed psychologist and a cultural fit check before use with patients.

scenarios.title: The quiet phone
scenarios.story: Your children are busy and rarely call. One evening you feel forgotten and a little low.

options.text: Call one of them, say you miss talking, and suggest a regular time to speak.
options.outcome: They are surprised and glad you called. You agree on a weekly call.
options.note: Reaches out and asks for what is needed. Explore what makes asking feel hard.

options.text: Wait for them to call and feel hurt.
options.outcome: The evening passes quietly, and the hurt sits with you.
options.note: Waiting avoids risk but also contact. Explore expectations about who should call first.

options.text: Tell yourself you are a burden and stop contacting them.
options.outcome: The distance grows and you feel more alone.
options.note: Feeling like a burden is a red flag to explore gently. Ask what the person believes about being a burden.

scenarios.keyMessage: Families often want contact but do not know the person is lonely. A simple request can change a lot.
scenarios.discussion: Who would you like to hear from more often, and what could you say to them?

scenarios.title: A new pain
scenarios.story: You notice a new pain and feel afraid of what the doctor might say.

options.text: Tell a family member, book the appointment, and ask someone to go with you.
options.outcome: It is scary, but having someone beside you helps, and you get clear answers.
options.note: Shares worry and seeks care. Explore who would be the best companion.

options.text: Wait and hope it goes away.
options.outcome: You worry privately for days and sleep badly.
options.note: Delay is common when frightened. Explore fears about bad news.

options.text: Keep it secret and avoid doctors completely.
options.outcome: The worry grows, and you feel more alone with it.
options.note: Avoidance can put health at risk. Explore what the person fears about doctors and being a burden.

scenarios.keyMessage: Worries shrink when shared. Seeing a doctor early gives more choices.
scenarios.discussion: Who could go with you to an appointment, and how would you ask them?

scenarios.title: The invitation
scenarios.story: A neighbour invites you to a small gathering. You feel tired and a little shy.

options.text: Go for a short while and tell them you may leave early.
options.outcome: You enjoy a cup of tea and a few conversations, and go home feeling lighter.
options.note: Balances energy and connection. Explore what made going possible.

options.text: Say you will see how you feel and then not go.
options.outcome: You rest at home but feel a little regret later.
options.note: Keeps options open but loses contact. Explore what makes saying yes hard.

options.text: Refuse and stay inside all week.
options.outcome: The days blur together and you feel lonelier.
options.note: Withdrawal feeds low mood. Explore what the person hopes for socially and what would make it easier.

scenarios.keyMessage: You do not have to stay long. A short visit is better than none.
scenarios.discussion: What small gathering or visit would feel manageable for you this week?
